This is a misunderstanding. The banks don’t need to “adopt APIs” in order for agents to be able to simply suggest & execute on moving their users’ funds away from accounts earning 0% interest to places they earn interest (whether that be money market funds, brokerage accounts, savings accounts that pay interest…whatever). The general idea doesn’t have anything to do with the financial system itself adopting AI, but rather AI being used by the depositors and it rationally suggesting more prudent decisions for savings. 

At the end of the day, there’s way too many banks that are getting away with offering essentially zero percent on savings. JPM maybe gets a pass because there will always be the argument that you give up the yield for the fact that if JPM goes under then the entire U.S. is cooked, but overall it’s a relatively new phenomenon and I would treat AI making it easier / more likely that depositors earn interest more as a return to normalcy than a departure.

Compared to Fusaka, Glamsterdam goes deeper and changes how Ethereum builds blocks and processes transactions.

Here are the biggest changes coming to @ethereum ↓

• ePBS: moves block-builder coordination into the protocol, so less reliance on trusted relays

• Access lists: map what each block touches, so validators can process unrelated transactions in parallel

• Gas repricing: fees match real computing and storage costs better, which makes growth more sustainable

• ETH logs: standard records for transfers and burns, easier for apps to track

• Bigger contracts: higher size limit, more room for devs to build

• Shared factory: apps can deploy at the same address across participating chains

FYI: Sepolia’s test was scheduled for today, and the Hoodi and mainnet dates are still TBD, so I’ll be watching for updates on those.

OR we're way earlier in this cycle than even I would have expected.

I'm strongly betting on the latter. and I'm pretty sure that not much is going to change about that until we've broken new ATHs and enter the parabolic zone.

Fun few years ahead.

I’m extremely sad to announce that Abstract is shutting down.

When we were just a three-person team building Frame I never could have imagined the two and half year journey I was about to embark on.

From the tireless nights preparing for launch, to mainnet going live in January 2025, and everything in between, this journey is one I will treasure for the rest of my life. Even though the outcome is not what we wanted, I am incredibly proud of everything we built at Abstract.

The Portal and Abstract Global Wallet made interacting with a blockchain feel seamless. That foundation led to a wave of unique apps, novel onchain experiences, and, most importantly, an incredibly passionate community that gave Abstract an identity and culture of its own.

But the truth is that the industry has changed significantly since the idea was first conceived in the summer of 2024, and Abstract was facing difficulties with our DeFi Ecosystem and liquidity on the chain.

We reached a crossroads of experiencing significant growth, but not having cemented product-market-fit,and that was becoming an issue from a business sustainability perspective.

A very difficult decision needed to be made. Abstract’s growth had stalled and the chain was simply not economically sustainable anymore despite our best efforts.

I am extremely grateful to the Igloo, Inc team who truly gave it their all to explore every angle and make Abstract work.

I want to take this time to thank the incredibly talented team I had the pleasure of working with over the last three years. Every single one of them poured their heart and soul into Abstract and together we created something truly special that pushed forward what onchain discovery and experiences could look like. It is the best team that I have ever worked with. I will always be proud of that.

I want to thank all of our partners and builders that worked with us to make Abstract such a unique, special place. Truly some of the most talented developers launched on Abstract and I know you will all kill it in your next chapter.

Most of all I want to thank the Abstract community for the support over these three years. I know there have been moments of frustration, but your passion and admiration for Abstract are what made it so special and helped create a culture that is incredibly rare in crypto. I truly wish this could have worked out for all of us.

Thank you for supporting the green chain ✳️

Back in March I sat down with @MartinDeVido, the guy who handed Claude a tomato plant and let it run the lights, the water and the sensors on its own. But its not one Claude. Its a team of them, each with a job. 

The one running the grow tent decides it needs a sensor it doesnt have, so it hands the spec to a circuit design Claude. A shopping Claude orders the parts. Martin mills it, assembles it and plugs it back into the system, which now has a sensor it designed for itself. 

He calls it the living factory.

The loop already runs from idea to physical object, with a human doing the assembly. 

Now picture it at factory scale, with the robots doing the assembly too...

The cost of intelligence is collapsing. The cost of energy is collapsing. The cost of a token, the cost of a watt, the amount of intelligence you get out of every unit of energy... all of it is falling at once.

And cheaper is what makes the whole thing go exponential. 

Jevons paradox... make something cheaper and the world finds a thousand new uses for it. Every time intelligence gets cheaper, we use more of it, which pays for the next round of getting cheaper. Wrights Law and Metcalfes Law running into each other.

We're at the very start of that and AI is already building AI...

Play it forward a few turns of the wheel and the speed of it goes beyond anything we can picture... intelligence being used in volumes we cant imagine, to build things we haven't even dreamed up yet.

Compute, energy, the rails the agents settle on. Thats where the value pools, and for the first time in history its something anyone can own a piece of.

We literally do that, and we first have an AI system that flags possible risk factors, and then we have a human clinician that then goes through and reviews those as well. Looking at OpenAI releasing hundreds of mathematical results, I think we really have to lead with empathy here.

When you’ve spent years learning a craft, whether it’s writing code, creating illustrations or doing mathematics, and suddenly a lot of what you do seems to be a prompt away, of course that’s disorienting. Your craft is how you define yourself, what you’re proud of, where you find flow, sometimes the thing that gives your day meaning. It’s a huge part of your identity.

And I get how this can lead to a pretty nihilistic feeling, like you wake up one morning and think, okay, if everything can just be prompted into existence, what am I supposed to do now? What am I getting better at? What is all this effort for?

Software engineers have been grappling with this for a while, and I expect more people will experience it as AI keeps accelerating. Writing a book, creating a movie, maybe someday helping solve a disease, more and more things we’ve spent our lives learning could feel a prompt away.

I think that progress is amazing, and I’m 100% confident we’ll find harder problems to work on and new crafts to fall in love with. But knowing that intellectually doesn’t make the sense of loss disappear, especially when the change happens this fast and feels this brutal.

We can celebrate the breakthroughs and still care about the millions of people trying to figure out where they fit and what gives their life meaning in a world becoming this intelligent. “You can do more now” might be true, but people also need time to process what they feel they’ve lost.
